displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that divine simplicity remains coherent if God's one intrinsic actuality is explanatorily sufficient for attributes, personal relations, free causation, and omniscience, while every plurality is either relationally opposed, conceptually grounded, or extrinsically terminated.

novelty.explanation: This integrates three transcript replies and repairs their shared need for a unified account of explanatory sufficiency.

premises.text: If something intrinsic to the ultimate source required a distinct unifying explanation, that source would not possess the radical explanatory independence demanded by aseity.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's aseity argument by making the unifying-explanation condition explicit.

premises.text: Distinct true predicates need not correspond to separable intrinsic constituents when one actuality supports different formally grounded descriptions through different explanatory roles or termini.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the compressed grounding bridge between analogical predication and objectively informative attribute distinctions.

premises.text: A relation can introduce real opposition through its terminus and direction without introducing another absolute constituent alongside the underlying reality that bears the relation.

novelty.explanation: This clarifies how relational reality could remain personally differentiating without functioning as another absolute component.

premises.text: One timeless cognitive act may determinately encompass every temporal and modal truth if its content is fixed by comprehensive self-understanding of divine causal power and every possible effect.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the transcript account by specifying a basis for intentional content beyond bare extrinsic predication.

premises.text: Freedom can concern which possible order receives an external causal terminus without requiring the intrinsic actuality of the agent to acquire a constituent or undergo improvement.

novelty.explanation: This is a new modal account distinguishing intrinsic agency from the contingent external termination of agency.

conclusion.text: Therefore, simplicity is coherent with the disputed commitments provided that formal grounding, relational opposition, and timeless modal content can perform their stated explanatory work without becoming additional intrinsic constituents.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately consolidates the repaired accounts while preserving their principal conditional burdens.

newArguments.title: Counterfactual profile without intrinsic plurality
newArguments.text: A simple actuality can possess a richly structured counterfactual profile without containing a matching inventory of intrinsic parts. One lawlike power, for example, may ground many conditionals because its possible termini differ, not because the power contains one constituent for every outcome. Applied cautiously to divine agency, the plurality of possible creations and knowledge attributions may track possible effects and truth conditions while the intrinsic explanatory source remains one. This does not prove simplicity, but it blocks an immediate inference from many determinate modal truths to many intrinsic cognitive items.

novelty.explanation: This newly uses counterfactual-profile structure to resist the inference from modal multiplicity to intrinsic composition.

newArguments.title: Reflexive content in an alone world
newArguments.text: The creationless-world objection can be answered by locating modal content in exhaustive divine self-knowledge rather than in nonexistent created facts. If God comprehends his causal capacity, the complete range of possible termini, and his actual nonexercise of that capacity, then truths about possible creation have an intrinsic foundation without becoming distinct intrinsic objects added to God. Their differentiation arises from formally distinct counterfactual relations within one reflexive act. The account still owes a theory of formal distinction, but it explains how contingent knowledge could remain available when no creature supplies an external truthmaker.

novelty.explanation: This directly repairs the pro reply at the point where the critic removes every created source of extrinsic differentiation.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that absolute simplicity remains inadequately explained whenever classical commitments require irreducibly different intrinsic truthmakers, personal asymmetries, modal contents, or epistemic relations that cannot all be assigned to creatures or conceptual description.

novelty.explanation: This unifies the critic's major challenges around a single demand for irreducible differentiation.

premises.text: Where two predicates differ in truth conditions and explanatory consequences, a satisfactory ontology must identify what grounds that contrast rather than merely classifying it as conceptual.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the critic's criterion by focusing application on explanatory truthmaker contrasts rather than every verbal distinction.

premises.text: Begottenness, begetting, and spiration encode asymmetric origins that appear indispensable to personal identity, so eliminating every intrinsic differentiator threatens to erase the realities those predicates express.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's asymmetric-predicate objection into an identity-based explanatory demand.

premises.text: If noncreation is genuinely possible, omniscience must distinguish actuality from unactualized possibilities even where no creature exists to provide an external differentiating terminus.

novelty.explanation: This retains the modal challenge while avoiding the stronger claim that each known truth is automatically a separate object.

premises.text: Knowledge of what is presently occurring has index-sensitive correctness conditions, and an account of immutable omniscience must explain how those conditions are cognitively available without succession.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the original argument by demanding an account of indexical availability instead of assuming intrinsic epistemic change.

premises.text: Appeals to formal, conceptual, or relational distinction require independent criteria showing when those distinctions explain real contrasts and when they merely rename unexplained plurality.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an explanatory-parity test applicable across attributes, persons, modality, and temporal knowledge.

conclusion.text: Therefore, the coherence of absolute simplicity remains conditional upon a detailed account of how one intrinsic actuality grounds every indispensable personal, modal, and epistemic contrast without explanatory loss or concealed composition.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion narrows the critical claim to an unmet explanatory condition rather than asserting a completed contradiction.

newArguments.title: The explanatory differentiation trilemma
newArguments.text: For each indispensable contrast, the simplicity defender appears to face three options: place its ground intrinsically in God, place it extrinsically in another reality, or treat it as conceptual description. The first option risks positive intrinsic differentiation; the second becomes unavailable for personal processions and in a creationless world; the third must explain why the contrast remains objective and causally or doctrinally consequential. This trilemma does not assume that every predicate names a part. Instead, it requires a uniform criterion showing which location supplies the contrast's truthmaker without sacrificing simplicity, realism, freedom, or omniscience.

novelty.explanation: This is a new organizing argument that tests all proposed distinctions through three exhaustive grounding locations.

newArguments.title: Indexical access without succession
newArguments.text: The temporal objection becomes stronger when framed around indexical access rather than straightforward acquisition. Complete knowledge seemingly includes not only tenseless truths about events but also which time is present relative to changing creatures. If presentness is wholly extrinsic, the account must explain how one immutable act determinately grounds every correct now-indexed attribution without any cognitive counterpart to the changing index. If presentness is intrinsic to divine knowledge, immutability is pressured. Either answer may be defensible, but the distinction account must provide a semantic and metaphysical mechanism rather than simply denying that God changes.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the changing-knowledge objection by replacing an assumed acquisition premise with a focused indexical-access dilemma.
